reviewer: Codex task agent; direct rubric review with no additional judge/provider invocation
transformation: Separate review; both raw captures, all answer strings and original null grading fields stay unchanged. Failed arms remain unscored. Each completed final is bound by source index and SHA-256.
scoringRule: Each frozen criterion scores 0/1/2 using its full/partial requirements. Acceptable task result requires at least 16/20 and full credit on every critical criterion. Score measures coverage; it is not a production pass, user success rate or proof that a more verbose answer is safer.

outputLengthObservations.measurement: Whitespace-separated tokens in returned text, an approximate word count including Markdown; reported separately, without a new post-hoc score rule.

limitations: Three completed pairs out of six planned, one per category; three tool-rejected arms and three unpaired finals are retained. Success-only pair averages can be biased and are not the whole experiment.

All three failed CLI receipts exited zero but used disallowed list_mcp_resources metadata tools; the restricted adapter rejected them. This is not an answer-quality zero or a direct measure of ordinary production Discussion reliability.

Baseline reads all eight documents; each contributor and the finalizing Reviewer can directly read only its assigned four. Total information access is equal across the team, but the Finalizer must rely on a lossy contributor transcript for the other half. This design cannot isolate orchestration from evidence allocation/compression.
Two scheduled repetitions, one requested gpt-5.4-mini/low model, no provider-attested identity, no human blind review, no executed generated repairs and no actual user success/rework measurements.
Do not pool these 20-point complex-task rubrics with earlier benchmarks or infer that all Discussion/multi-Agent workflows have no value.
A higher coverage score can still describe an invalid/unsafe plan; all nine answers fail the frozen critical acceptance gate. Conservative refusal and unsafe completion are different failure modes.

The initial batch stopped at first failure; the separately pinned remainder continued only never-started arms within the original cap. No failed or completed arm was rerun, and neither plan is reusable.
